correctness.rationale: All facets for perfect complete multipartite graphs are clique-indexed and have norm sqrt(4|C|+1). Optimality of t=1/sqrt(4r+1) forces maximal-clique equations; varying one class at a time implies x_v=a_j and z=2sum a_j. Remaining inequalities reduce to omitted-set sums bounded by beta_t. beta_0=0 and strict convexity imply beta_t>t beta_1 for t>=2, proving exactly |a_j|<=h. This gives exhaustive, strict contact levels; Gram determinant gives intrinsic r-volume. The actual bundled script independently checked 32 tuples, 2520 centers and 1770 scalar inequalities with finite precision, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The full set of maximum balls, not merely the maximum radius, is a natural geometric invariant. Its exact r-dimensional parallelotope for all class-size profiles, strict absence of all lower-rank facet contacts and the complete boundary contact census are structural facts not implied by known scalar and origin-contact formulae. Intrinsic optimizer-volume depends on class sizes even though the radius and parameter cube side lengths do not; this is a meaningful metric distinction.
